keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox "Dates: ca. 5,440 BCE to 460 CE", range New Mexico and Colorado. The two states are drawn whole (1,878 land cells, about 475,000 km2) less the south-west of New Mexico that the Cochise page gives to the Cochise; this overstates a tradition known from sites near Denver, the Upper Gunnison, Mesa Verde and the Arroyo Cuervo area of north-west New Mexico. No area figure is given.

ledger.note: 5440 BCE: the Oshara tradition begins in New Mexico and Colorado. Infobox "Dates: ca. 5,440 BCE to 460 CE" and "Geographical range: New Mexico, Colorado"; the Jay phase is given as "7,450 to 6,750 years before present". Year and states are the page's; leaving out the south-west corner of New Mexico is the dossier's.

4800 BCE: the Bajada phase of the Oshara. "Bajada phase (6,750 to 5,150 years BP)"; 6,750 BP is 4800 BCE (BP counted from 1950). The San Jose phase is given as "6,750 to 3,750 years BP", which overlaps the Bajada and is not used.
800 BCE: the En Medio phase of the Oshara. "En Medio phase (2,750 to 1,550 years BP)", 2,750 BP being 800 BCE; the page says it "was roughly analogous to the southwestern Basketmaker culture".

ledger.note: 460 CE: the Oshara tradition gives way to the Ancient Pueblo People. Infobox "Dates: ca. 5,440 BCE to 460 CE" and "Followed by: Ancient Pueblo People"; the page does not say what land passed.

certainty.note: No border is recorded; New Mexico and Colorado are the infobox range, not a frontier.

sources.title: Oshara tradition
sources.note: Infobox Dates ca. 5,440 BCE to 460 CE, range New Mexico and Colorado, Preceded by Picosa, Followed by Ancient Pueblo People; phases Jay, Bajada, San Jose, En Medio.

sources.title: Archaic period (North America)
sources.note: Archaic 8000-1000 BC; Middle Archaic mounds from 3500 BC; Old Copper complex 4000-1000 BC; Oshara 5500 BC-500 AD; Cochise.

notes: Oshara tradition, a Southwestern Archaic tradition. Phase dates are in years BP on the page; converted with BP = years before 1950. Phases Irving is not on the page. San Jose "6,750 to 3,750 years BP" overlaps Bajada "6,750 to 5,150" (page inconsistency; no San Jose event). The tradition runs past the 3400 BCE horizon because nothing else draws New Mexico and Colorado until the Ancestral Puebloans (no dossier; slug ancient-pueblo-peoples suggested). The Picosa culture (predecessor, infobox) has no dossier and no dates here. The border with the Cochise (south-west New Mexico) is the dossier's: a 150 km disc at 32.77 N, 108.28 W stands for the Cochise page's "western New Mexico". Archaic-period page: "5500 BC-500 AD: Oshara tradition ... arises in north-central New Mexico".
